    • Google

      Firm · Accelerator vendors

      Designs the Tensor Processing Unit (TPU), and announced the eighth generation, the TPU 8t and TPU 8i, in April 2026. It uses TPUs in its own data centers and offers them to cloud customers. Broadcom and MediaTek work with it on the physical design, which turns a chip design into a layout, and on manufacturing at TSMC.

    • Google TPU 8i (Zebrafish)

      AI chip

      Google split its eighth TPU generation into two chips, one for training and one for inference. The TPU 8i is the inference chip. It replaces Ironwood’s four SparseCores with a dedicated Collectives Acceleration Engine (CAE), which cuts on-chip latency for collectives, the operations in which chips share results, about fivefold. It also carries 384 MB of on-chip Vmem. Google says each TPU 8i chip has “two Tensor Cores (TC) on-core dies and one CAE on the chiplet die”. That wording names core dies and a separate chiplet die but gives no die count. So the die-count field is empty, and the package drawing shows one core die and one chiplet die. The TPU 8t training chip has 216 GB of HBM at 6,528 GB/s, 12.6 PFLOPS of FP4 and a 3D torus reaching 9,600 chips. Google has named no design partner, node, packaging, HBM generation, stack count, power figure or availability date for either chip. SemiAnalysis puts the eighth generation on TSMC N3. Google says both eighth-generation chips will be generally available later in 2026. Its Cloud TPU release notes carry no such entry as of 27 September 2026.

    • Google TPU 8t

      AI chip

      Google split its eighth TPU generation into two chips, one for training and one for inference. The TPU 8t is the training chip. It keeps SparseCores for embeddings and uses an Arm Axion host CPU. Google publishes HBM capacity, bandwidth, on-chip memory, FP4 peak and pod size. It publishes no node, die count, package, stack count, power or availability date, beyond saying the chip will be generally available later in 2026. SemiAnalysis puts the eighth generation on TSMC N3

    • Google TPU v4

      AI chip

      TPU v4 is the generation that made TPUs credible outside Google. It is also the only TPU with a published power figure. Google’s ISCA 2023 paper reports 90 W at idle and a measured minimum, mean and maximum draw of 121, 170 and 192 W, and the power figure in the table is that measured maximum. Each chip has two TensorCores and HBM2 memory. As of October 2026, Google’s Cloud TPU documentation names the HBM generation for this part and for no later TPU. The chips connect in a 3D mesh, which Google says can be configured as a 3D torus, a mesh whose edges wrap around, on some slice shapes. Google’s TPU pages give only compute, memory and fabric numbers. Its ISCA 2023 paper on TPU v4 adds the rest: 7 nm, 22 billion transistors, one die with four HBM stacks, and six chip-to-chip links at 50 GB/s. The table above uses those figures. Epoch AI records a 7 nm process and a 340 W thermal design power (TDP) for the part. A TDP is a design rating, but the 192 W is Google’s own measured maximum, so the table leaves Epoch’s figure out.

    • Google TPU v5e

      AI chip

      Google describes Cloud TPU v5e as a combined training and inference product. Its specification table lists an expected performance per total cost of ownership of 0.65x, against 1 in the v6e table. Its total processing performance sits under the 4,800 export threshold, yet a pod of 256 chips delivers 50.63 PFLOPs. Google publishes compute, memory and fabric numbers for its TPUs and nothing else: no foundry, no process node, no die area, no transistor count, no package type and no HBM stack count. Those fields are empty except the die area. The 325 mm² figure is Epoch AI’s, and it is shown because the export-control arithmetic depends on it.

    • Google TPU v5p

      AI chip

      The training TPU of the pre-Ironwood era. Its pod of 8,960 chips, linked in a 3D torus to work as one system, was the largest such system Google had built at the time. Each chip carries two TensorCores and four SparseCores. Its FP8 rate equals its BF16 rate. That is the clearest sign that the v5 generation was designed before chipmakers competed mainly on low-precision throughput. Google publishes compute, memory and fabric numbers for its TPUs and nothing else. The N5 node here comes from SemiAnalysis. The other silicon fields are empty.

    • Google TPU v6e (Trillium)

      AI chip

      The last TPU before Ironwood. Google does not name the memory type. SemiAnalysis gives two stacks of HBM3, which is consistent with 1,638 GB/s across 32 GB. Google publishes compute, memory and fabric numbers for its TPUs and nothing else. The N5 node and the stack count here come from SemiAnalysis. The other silicon fields are empty. Epoch AI estimates the power draw at about 380 W. Because that is an estimate and Google publishes no figure, the power field is empty.

    • Google TPU v7 (Ironwood)

      AI chip

      Google’s seventh-generation TPU (Tensor Processing Unit). It is built for inference, and its superpod links 9,216 chips in a 3D torus. For a TPU, Google is unusually specific about the package. The Cloud TPU documentation states that Ironwood is composed of two distinct chiplets, each a self-contained unit with one TensorCore, two SparseCores and 96 GB of HBM. The architecture post names eight HBM3E stacks for 192 GiB at a peak 7.4 TB/s, which is the 7,380 GB/s in the documentation. So each chiplet has four stacks, and the package drawing shows them that way. Google still publishes no node, die area, transistor count, package, HBM supplier or power figure. The N3E node shown comes from SemiAnalysis.

      Term

      graphics processing unit, GPUs

      A processor originally built to draw video game images by doing thousands of simple calculations at once. Neural networks turned out to need the same kind of arithmetic, so the GPU became the default AI processor.

      Nvidia used 60.3 percent of all CoWoS packaging in 2025, on Epoch AI’s estimate. The US required a license for Nvidia’s H20 in April 2025. Since January 2026 it has reviewed applications to sell the H200 to buyers in China case by case.

      Firm · Accelerator vendors

      Designs the Language Processing Unit (LPU), an inference chip that uses large on-chip SRAM and no HBM, and whose compiler schedules every operation in advance. It sells few chips. Instead it runs AI models in its own cloud and charges customers per token of text processed.

    • Groq LPU

      AI chip

      The LPU is the purest SRAM-only design in production. All of its memory is SRAM on the chip itself, with no HBM at all. It runs a fully deterministic VLIW pipeline, in which the timing of every step is fixed in advance. The design works only when hundreds of chips are wired together as one machine. SemiAnalysis reports that its 14 nm first generation was fabricated at GlobalFoundries and packaged in the United States. The 230 MB of SRAM and the 215 W shown above are for the first-generation GroqChip. Epoch AI recorded them from a Groq product brief whose link no longer works. Groq’s current pages give neither a power figure nor a per-chip SRAM capacity. Its rack figure of 128 GB across 256 LPUs implies 500 MB per chip on the current part. Groq publishes no package type and no price. Its ISCA 2020 paper gives the first-generation chip 26.8 billion transistors.

    • gross margin

      Term

      The share of a sale left over after paying what it cost to make the thing, before research, sales and overheads are counted. A 70 percent gross margin means $70 of every $100 of revenue is left after manufacturing cost.

      Gross margin shows which firms have pricing power. In quarters ending June to September 2026, Micron’s was 86.8 percent and Nvidia’s 75.0 percent. The assembly and test houses Amkor and ASE were at 16.8 to 27.3 percent, counting ASE’s packaging and test segment alone.

      Read it in The Economics of AI Chips

    • HBM

      Term

      high bandwidth memory, high-bandwidth memory, HBM3E, HBM4, HBM4E, HBM stack, HBM stacks, memory stacks, stacked memory

      Stacked memory built for AI chips. Up to sixteen memory chips are stacked into a cube and wired together through copper-filled holes made in each chip before stacking. The cube sits a few millimeters from the processor. It holds the model the chip is running, the numbers called weights, and hands them to the processor over 1,024 or more wires at once.

      To write each word of an answer, the chip reads the whole model from this memory, along with the record of the conversation so far. A larger model or a longer conversation needs more memory, so the size and speed of HBM usually set how many people one chip can serve. HBM is the largest line in the bill of materials of an Nvidia B200. SK hynix, Samsung and Micron make nearly all of it.

      Read it in Memory and HBM

    • Huawei (HiSilicon) Ascend 910B

      AI chip

      The 910B is Huawei’s domestic answer to Nvidia’s A100, and it shows that export controls have an effect. CSET finds that Huawei needed at least two years to redesign the part for SMIC, the Chinese foundry. CSET also finds that Huawei cut the number of active AI cores between the first and second generations, most likely because of yield or capacity limits on SMIC’s 7 nm line. CSET dates the series to 2022. No allowed source gives a first-shipment date, so that field is empty. The 910B ships in several grades, from a 910B4 at 32 GB and 800 GB/s to a 910B1 at 64 GB and 1.6 TB/s. The figures above are for the top of that range. SemiAnalysis places the chip between the A100 and the H100 in performance. Huawei publishes no die area, transistor count, package detail or per-chip datasheet.

    • Huawei (HiSilicon) Ascend 910C

      AI chip

      The 910C is the clearest case in the industry of a domestic chip built largely from imported dies. SemiAnalysis judges that most 910B and 910C dies were made on TSMC N7 and reached Huawei through Sophgo, another Chinese chip designer, before TSMC stopped supplying Sophgo. Huawei’s answer to weak per-chip performance is scale. Its CloudMatrix 384 system links 384 chips and beats Nvidia’s GB200 NVL72 rack on total BF16 compute, but it uses about four times the power. Huawei publishes no datasheet for the part. The 781 TFLOPS above is SemiAnalysis’s system figure, 300 PFLOPS of dense BF16, divided across 384 chips. SemiAnalysis names Samsung as the source of the HBM2E Huawei stockpiled. The 128 GB of HBM2E, the 3.2 TB/s and the 700 W come from Epoch AI’s hardware database. Epoch’s own citations for them mix a Huawei keynote and SemiAnalysis with a market-research outlet.

    • Huawei (HiSilicon) Ascend 950PR

      AI chip

      The 950PR is the first Huawei accelerator to ship with Huawei’s own high-bandwidth memory (HBM) instead of stockpiled Korean HBM. That is the most consequential claim on Huawei’s roadmap. Huawei sells the chip as the Atlas 350 card, which it says can run alone or in groups of four linked by UnifiedBus, Huawei’s chip-to-chip connection. Huawei dated the 950PR to the first quarter of 2026. Huawei names HiBL 1.0 as the memory. The card’s spec table gives 112 GB at 1.4 TB/s, well short of the 144 GB at 4 TB/s Huawei promises for the 950DT. Node, die count, die area, package and price are unpublished.

    • hybrid bonding

      Term

      direct bond interconnect, SoIC, Foveros Direct, copper pad to copper pad

      Joining two chips by bonding their copper pads, and the glass-like insulator around them, directly to each other, with no solder in between. Removing the solder lets connections be packed much more tightly and shortens the path heat has to travel out.

      An SK hynix tech note puts microbumps about 20 micrometers apart and hybrid-bonded pads under 1 micrometer apart. It expects full-scale use in HBM at HBM4E or HBM5, where stacks are projected to pass twenty layers.

      Read it in Advanced Packaging

    • hydrogen fluoride

      Term

      hydrofluoric acid, HF, ultra-high-purity hydrofluoric acid, high-purity hydrogen fluoride

      Hydrogen fluoride is a gas that dissolves glass, and hydrofluoric acid is its solution in water. Fabs use both to strip oxide layers and clean wafers between steps. Like other cleaning chemicals, it is purified until metal impurities are down to parts per trillion.

      When Japan put it under individual export licenses for South Korea in 2019, Japan’s exports of it to South Korea fell 87.9 percent. South Korea bought more from the United States and Taiwan and made more at home.

      Read it in Chemicals, Gases and Photoresist

      They pay for the AI buildout. Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle spent $448.2 billion of capital in 2025, the sum of Epoch AI’s quarterly figures.

      Read it in Data Centers and Power

      SMEE, the established Chinese scanner maker, is strongest in i-line, and even there it holds about 4 percent of the world market.

It supplies substrates for large AI packages and is expanding capacity, first mainly at its Gama plant, which it said in August 2026 would start operating in stages from the end of fiscal 2027.

      Firm · Equipment subsystems

      Designs and builds the gas panels, weldments and chemical delivery modules that route process gases into etch and deposition chambers. It is an outsourced manufacturing partner to the large tool vendors.

      Term

      integrated device manufacturer, integrated device maker, integrated device makers

      A chip company that both designs its products and manufactures them in its own factories. Intel, Samsung and Micron are examples.

      An integrated maker that also makes chips for other companies competes with its own customers. Its own products take the best capacity, so fewer customers trust it with a flagship design.

      Read it in Foundries and Fabs

    • Iluvatar CoreX

      Firm · Accelerator vendors

    • Imagination Technologies

      Licenses GPU and neural network accelerator IP for edge and automotive silicon. Its ownership by a China-linked fund made it an early test case for technology transfer scrutiny in the UK.

    • immersion lithography

      Term

      immersion DUV, ArF immersion, immersion scanner, immersion scanners, immersion tools, immersion DUV scanners, immersion deep-ultraviolet

      Immersion lithography prints with a thin layer of ultrapure water between the scanner’s lens and the wafer. The water lets the lens focus light at a wider angle than air allows, so the same light prints finer lines. It is the most advanced form of deep ultraviolet lithography, one step below extreme ultraviolet.

      Dutch export licensing covers the most advanced immersion scanners. Reuters reported in July 2026, citing one unnamed source, that a Chinese state-owned firm had started producing its own immersion scanners.

      Read it in Lithography

    • IMS Nanofabrication

      Firm · Photomasks

      Builds the multi-beam electron mask writers that pattern EUV masks with hundreds of thousands of parallel beamlets. On CSET’s count it led the market for all electron-beam mask writers in 2025. NuFlare is the only other maker of multi-beam writers.

    • in-country transfer

      Export control

      transfer (in-country)

      A change in the end use or the end user of an item inside one foreign country, defined at 15 CFR 734.16. Nothing crosses a border. A server legally imported into a country for one customer is transferred when it is resold, or repurposed, for another.

      Controls on in-country transfers catch hardware diverted after it has arrived. So a license granted for a named Chinese customer does not cover the hardware if it passes to someone else. Reexports and in-country transfers of advanced chips to Macau or Country Group D:5 keep a presumption of denial, meaning a license will normally be refused (91 FR 1684). That holds even where an export from the United States would be reviewed case by case (91 FR 1684).

      Read it in Who Controls the Chain

    • indium phosphide

      Term

      InP, indium

      Indium phosphide is a crystal grown from the metal indium and phosphorus. It gives off light when current passes through it, which silicon cannot do efficiently. The lasers inside the fastest optical modules are made of it.

      China produced about 70 percent of the world’s indium in 2025. In February 2025 it put indium under new export restrictions and began requiring export permits for indium phosphide substrates. In March 2026 Nvidia agreed to invest $2 billion each in Coherent and Lumentum, alongside purchase commitments for their lasers.

      Read it in Systems and Networking

    • inference

      Term

      inference chip, inference chips, inference accelerator, inference accelerators, training and inference

      Inference is running a finished AI model to answer requests, such as a prompt. Training, a run of weeks on a cluster of accelerators, builds the model first. To write each word of an answer, the chip reads the whole model from memory, does a little arithmetic and waits for the next read. Training reuses each number it fetches, so it fetches little and computes a lot.

      In inference, memory size and speed usually set how many people one chip can serve.

      Read it in Memory and HBM

      Firm · Power and cooling

      Supplies the MOSFETs, gallium nitride devices and power stages used from the grid connection through the rack power shelf to the point-of-load regulator. It is the largest power semiconductor maker, according to Omdia figures Infineon published in August 2026. Those figures give it 17.3 percent of the $32.5 billion market for power discretes and modules in 2025, against 7.2 percent for onsemi.

    • InfiniBand

      Term

      Quantum-2, Quantum-X800

      InfiniBand is a networking standard long used in supercomputers, with low delay and no dropped packets. AI clusters relied on it to link thousands of servers before Ethernet caught up, and Nvidia still sells both.

      The choice between InfiniBand and Ethernet decides who sells the switch chips. Broadcom has doubled the bandwidth of its Ethernet switch chips with each generation since 2019.

      Read it in Systems and Networking

    • Innolight Technology

      Firm · Optics and photonics

      中际旭创

      A world-leading maker of high-speed optical transceiver modules for data centers, shipping 800G and 1.6T modules to hyperscalers. AI clusters need one or more optical modules per accelerator.

    • Inpria

      Firm · Photoresist

      Developed tin-oxide EUV resists that absorb EUV photons far more efficiently than organic chemically amplified resists. Higher absorption cuts the light dose needed and sharpens resolution on High-NA EUV tools.

    • Intel

      Firm · Accelerator vendors

      Designs Xeon server CPUs and the Gaudi accelerator line. Xeon chips are still the host CPUs in most AI clusters. Its product business is separate from Intel Foundry, the company’s manufacturing arm.

    • Intel Foundry

      Firm · Foundry

      Intel’s manufacturing arm, running the 18A process with RibbonFET gate-all-around and PowerVia backside power, plus EMIB and Foveros packaging. Most of its output is still Intel’s own chips. Outside customers provided only $293 million of its $5.765 billion of segment revenue in the quarter to 27 June 2026.

    • Intel Gaudi 2

      AI chip

      With Gaudi 2, Intel made the Ethernet choice that Gaudi 3 inherited. Gaudi 2 has 24 RDMA network interfaces (NICs) on the package, so a Gaudi cluster needs no proprietary cabling and no InfiniBand. It also carries 48 MB of local SRAM and hardware video decoders that let it run its own pre-processing. Intel positioned Gaudi 2 against the A100 but never gave it a datasheet of its own. So the compute figures come from the comparison table in Intel’s Gaudi 3 white paper, which records Gaudi 2 at 432 TFLOPS BF16 and 865 TFLOPS FP8. Epoch AI gives the foundry as TSMC and the die as 826 mm². The table above uses the foundry. It leaves out the die area, because 826 mm² is exactly the A100 figure and Epoch’s citation for the row is an archived page, with no primary document behind it. Intel publishes no die count, die area, transistor count or memory supplier. Its Gaudi 3 white paper gives Gaudi 2 six HBM2E stacks.

    • Intel Gaudi 3

      AI chip

      Gaudi 3 is an AI accelerator that Intel sells on the open market. It uses standard Ethernet both to link the eight cards on a baseboard and to link baseboards together, with 24 RoCE ports of 200 gigabits on the package. Intel’s next announced inference part is Crescent Island, a data center GPU with 160 GB of LPDDR5X. Intel expects customer sampling in the second half of 2026. Intel publishes no die area, transistor count, package dimensions, HBM supplier or per-chip list price for Gaudi 3. Its white paper names TSMC 5 nm as the process.

    • interposer

      Term

      interposers, silicon interposer, silicon carrier

      A layer of wiring with no transistors, used as a miniature circuit board underneath several chips so they can be connected at a density no ordinary board could reach. It is either one piece of silicon or layers of fine copper wiring, often with small silicon bridges.

      HBM connects over 1,024 or 2,048 wires, too many for a resin board, so memory and logic sit together on an interposer. Its area caps how much fits in one package. In April 2026 TSMC was producing CoWoS at 5.5 times the reticle, the largest area a lithography machine prints in one exposure.

      Read it in Advanced Packaging

    • Inventec

      Firm · Systems and servers

      英業達

      Builds AI and general purpose servers for cloud operators and OEMs, with manufacturing in Taiwan, Mexico, the Czech Republic and Malaysia.

    • ion implantation

      Term

      ion implanter, ion implanters, implant, implant layers, implantation

      A way of changing how silicon conducts by firing atoms into it. An ion implanter shoots charged atoms of boron, phosphorus or arsenic into the wafer, where they lodge just under the surface. The patches they land in then conduct the way the design needs.

      Every modern chip process relies on it. Implanters are export-controlled. In February 2026 Applied Materials agreed to pay a penalty of about $252 million over implanters shipped to a Chinese customer on the Entity List.

      Read it in Foundries and Fabs

    • IP

      Term

      silicon IP, IP blocks, licensed blocks, licensed circuit blocks, semiconductor IP, IP catalog, intellectual property

      In chip design, IP, short for intellectual property, means a ready-made block of circuitry, such as a processor core or a memory interface, that a design house licenses. Arm sells processor IP, and other firms sell the blocks that talk to memory, PCIe or another chiplet.

      Each licensed block must be proven on a new process before a chip can use it. The memory interface is a demanding one, because it has to hold its timing across thousands of solder bumps into a stacked memory die.

      Read it in Chip Design, EDA and IP

    • is-informed letter

      Export control

      is informed letter, is-informed letters, by letter

      A letter from BIS to one named company imposing a license requirement on a specific export, without any rule being published. BIS’s power to send one is written into the regulations themselves, for example 15 CFR 744.23(b), which lets BIS inform a person individually, with no amendment to the EAR.

      It imposes a control at once, with no published rule. BIS imposed the April 2025 license requirement for Nvidia’s H20 this way, and the public learned of it from Nvidia’s own filing.

      Read it in Who Controls the Chain

      Makers now ship HBM4 faster than the standard’s 8 Gb/s per pin. Samsung’s runs at 11.7, SK hynix’s above 10 and Micron’s above 11. Each customer runs its own qualification tests, so meeting the standard does not by itself win an order.

      A kilowatt is a thousand watts. A megawatt is a thousand kilowatts, and a gigawatt a thousand megawatts, about the output of one large power station. A GB300 NVL72 rack draws up to 142 kilowatts. The largest data center campuses are planned in gigawatts.

      AI deals are now counted in gigawatts too, as when OpenAI and Broadcom announced 10 gigawatts of accelerators. Power equipment now arrives more slowly than the chips.

    • known-good die

      Term

      KGD, good die, good dies, known good die

      A bare chip tested thoroughly enough, before assembly, to be trusted inside something expensive. In an ordinary product a faulty chip wastes one chip. Inside a package that joins a dozen expensive pieces, one bad die throws away all of them.

      As packages grow toward about ten large compute dies and 20 memory stacks, a bad die found only after assembly scraps more parts. So chipmakers move testing and burn-in, running chips hot to force early failures, back onto the wafer.

      Read it in Test and Assembly

      Makes batch vertical furnaces and batch ALD systems that process dozens of wafers at once. Memory makers use them widely for DRAM and 3D NAND film steps where throughput matters more than single-wafer control.

    • KrF

      KrF is krypton fluoride, the gas in an older lithography laser that shines at 248 nanometers. KrF scanners print the coarser layers of a chip, where lines are far apart.

      KrF tools print coarser layers such as implant layers. ASML sold 78 of them in 2025, and Canon also makes them.

      The largest supplier of plasma etch systems. According to CSET, it had 41.1 percent of the $21.9 billion dry etch tool market in 2025, against 23.4 percent for Tokyo Electron.     • laminate

      Term

      laminates, copper-clad laminate, copper-clad laminates, low-loss laminate, core laminate

      A laminate is a stiff sheet made by pressing glass cloth and resin together, usually with copper foil bonded to its faces. It is the material a circuit board or a substrate core is cut from. A low-loss laminate absorbs little of the signal passing through the wires on it.

      How much signal the laminate absorbs has become a main design limit on the boards that link GPUs.

      Read it in Substrates and PCBs

    • large power transformer

      Term

      large power transformers, transformer, transformers, switchgear, substation

      A large power transformer is a machine that changes grid electricity from one voltage to another, for example from transmission voltage down to a level a data center can use. Switchgear is the heavy switching and protection equipment around it. Together they make up the substation at the gate of the campus.

      In 2024 lead times of 36 months were commonly quoted, against under a year before the pandemic. Of the units put into US service in 2019, 82 percent were imported.

      Read it in Data Centers and Power

In October 2025 it launched the ACTIS A200HiT series, which it says triples the A150’s inspection speed. These tools detect printable phase defects, flaws in a mask’s reflective layers that DUV-based mask inspection cannot find.

    • lead time

      Term

      lead times, delivery time

      Lead time is the wait between placing an order and receiving it. A wafer clears a leading-edge fab in months, while in 2024 a large power transformer commonly took three years.

      Chip supply and power equipment are both constrained. Micron said in its report for the quarter to May 2026 that AI-driven memory and storage growth was outpacing industry supply. Waits for large power equipment run to years.

      Read it in Data Centers and Power

    • leading edge

      Term

      leading-edge, at the leading edge, advanced node, advanced nodes, advanced-node

      The leading edge is the newest generation of chipmaking process in volume production. In 2026 that means the 3 nm and 2 nm nodes, made only by TSMC, Samsung and Intel. A leading-edge chip is one built on it.

      Gate-all-around transistors are the design used at 2 nm, and only TSMC, Intel and Samsung make them in volume. In 2024 the United States put a worldwide license requirement on the technology for building them.

      Read it in Foundries and Fabs

      Builds AI servers and its Neptune warm-water liquid cooling systems, selling into enterprises and research computing worldwide from plants in China, Hungary, Mexico and the US.

    • LG Innotek

      Firm · Substrates and PCBs

      엘지이노텍

      Entered high-end flip-chip BGA substrates in 2022 with a plant in Gumi, adding a third Korean source alongside Samsung Electro-Mechanics. Its larger business is optical modules for smartphones.

    • license exception

      Export control

      license exception

      A written carve-out in export rules that lets a shipment go without an individual license, if it meets stated conditions. The ones that matter for AI chips and chipmaking tools are NAC and ACA (15 CFR 740.8), HBM (740.25), AIA and LPP (740.27 and 740.29), IEC (740.24) and RPL (740.10). AIA and LPP let the top band of accelerators ship to allies, and elsewhere in small volumes. IEC covers countries that adopt matching controls, and RPL covers servicing and spare parts.

      Exceptions let the US government adjust its controls without rewriting them and ease the rules for allies. License Exception IEC, added in September 2024, covers exports to and by countries that have put equivalent controls in place (89 FR 72926).

      Read it in Who Controls the Chain

    • License Exception ACA

      Export control

      ACA, Advanced Computing Authorized

      An export rule that lets AI chips other than top-band data center chips ship to most of the world with no license and no advance notice. It covers the same chips as its companion exception NAC, and every destination except Macau, Country Group D:5 and firms headquartered in either. The top-band data center chips in ECCN 3A090.a are excluded. BIS split it from NAC at 15 CFR 740.8 in April 2024. The AI Diffusion rule widened it in January 2025 to the whole world outside Macau and D:5.

      It lets these chips reach most of the world with no license or advance notice. NAC keeps a notice requirement for Macau and D:5. Before April 2024 NAC did both jobs, so an older table that shows one exception describes what is now two.

      Read it in Who Controls the Chain

    • License Exception ACM

      Export control

      ACM, Advanced Compute Manufacturing

      License Exception ACM, for Advanced Compute Manufacturing, lets controlled AI chips and related items go without a license to private-sector firms that develop, make or store them. The items must be bound for customers outside Macau and Country Group D:5. It was created alongside License Exceptions AIA and LPP.

      It keeps the AI Diffusion rule’s worldwide license requirement from catching chips that are only passing through factories and warehouses on their way to an eligible customer.

      Read it in Who Controls the Chain

    • License Exception AIA

      Export control

      AIA, Artificial Intelligence Authorization

      License Exception AIA, for Artificial Intelligence Authorization, lets the top band of AI chips ship without a license to nineteen destinations. They are listed in supplement no. 5 to part 740, and the United States is among them. The AI Diffusion rule created it in January 2025 as the exception inside a worldwide license requirement.

      BIS said in May 2025 that it would not enforce the AI Diffusion rule. But the rule was never repealed, so AIA still stands in the regulations. BIS says it enforces the worldwide requirement only for Country Groups D:1, D:4 and D:5 and for firms headquartered in D:5 or Macau.

      Read it in Who Controls the Chain

    • License Exception HBM

      Export control

      An export rule that lets high bandwidth memory go to a packaging site with no license, to be packaged beside a chip. It applies if the memory’s bandwidth density is below 3.3 GB/s per square millimeter, measured over the area of the package or stack. The exporter must be headquartered in the United States or Country Group A:5. If the memory is bound for Macau or Country Group D:5, the chip’s designer must buy it. The stacks must go straight to the packaging site. It does not cover packaging at a facility in Macau or D:5 that also makes advanced-node chips. It sits at 15 CFR 740.25.

      It lets Chinese packaging houses stay in the supply chain of American and allied chip designers. But a sale of the same stacks to a Chinese buyer still needs a license. HBM needs a license only for Macau and Country Group D:5, and the exception was written into the December 2024 rule that first controlled HBM (89 FR 96790).

      Read it in Who Controls the Chain

    • License Exception LPP

      Export control

      LPP, Low Processing Performance

      An export rule that lets a buyer almost anywhere receive a capped amount of top-band AI chips each year without a license. The cap is 26,900,000 TPP, the export rules’ measure of computing power, per ultimate consignee per calendar year. Macau, Country Group D:5 and firms headquartered in either are excluded, and it does not cover transfers within a country. The AI Diffusion rule created it in January 2025, at 15 CFR 740.29.

      It lets buyers outside the nineteen destinations in supplement no. 5 to part 740 take top AI chips in small amounts with no license application. BIS said in May 2025 that it would not enforce the AI Diffusion rule, but it withdrew none of the text. So LPP still stands in the regulations beside the rule’s other exceptions, AIA and ACM, and the nineteen-destination list.

      Read it in Who Controls the Chain

    • License Exception NAC

      Export control

      NAC, Notified Advanced Computing

      An export rule that lets AI chips other than top-band data center chips ship to Macau and Country Group D:5, and to firms headquartered there, with no license. The exporter must notify BIS at least 25 calendar days ahead, and the shipment can go if BIS does not say a license is needed. The top-band data center chips in ECCN 3A090.a and the memory in 3A090.c are excluded. It sits at 15 CFR 740.8.

      It lets these chips reach the restricted destinations without a license application. Since April 2024 section 740.8 has held two exceptions, NAC for the restricted destinations and ACA for everywhere else.

      Read it in Who Controls the Chain

    • liquid cooling

      Term

      direct-to-chip cooling, cold plate cooling, cold plate, cold plates, liquid-cooled, direct-to-chip liquid, direct liquid cooling

      Taking heat out of a processor by pumping liquid through a cold plate on the chip package, instead of blowing air across a finned heatsink. A building loop then carries the heat outdoors.

      Nvidia’s GB300 NVL72 rack is liquid cooled, and its Rubin platform is entirely liquid cooled. Nvidia says every cloud provider and data center operator building for Rubin is moving to liquid cooling.

      Read it in Data Centers and Power

    • lithography

      Term

      photolithography

      Printing a circuit pattern onto a wafer by shining light through a patterned plate and projecting a shrunken image of it onto a light-sensitive coating. It works like photography at the scale of nanometers, repeated once for every layer of the chip.

      Only one company, ASML, makes the machines for its finest layers, and those layers set how densely transistors and wires pack.

      Read it in Lithography

    • logic chip

      Term

      logic chips, logic die, logic dies

      A logic chip is one that computes, such as a processor, a graphics processor or an AI accelerator. Memory chips, such as DRAM and NAND flash, store data instead.

      US export rules set separate lines for logic and memory. The October 2022 rule covered equipment for fabs in China making logic chips at 16/14 nm or below. It also covered fabs making DRAM at 18 nm half-pitch or below, or NAND with 128 or more layers. ASML’s 2025 system sales were €16,054.1 million to logic chipmakers and €8,420.2 million to memory makers.

      Read it in Foundries and Fabs

      A lot is the batch of wafers a fab moves through its machines together, usually 25 in one sealed carrier. Recipes, inspections and yield are tracked lot by lot.

      A fab decides how many wafers in each lot it can afford to inspect. That choice sets how much it spends on process control, the measuring that keeps each step on target.

    • Malaysia

      Country

      Test and assembly, the last stage before the server

    • Marvell Technology

      Firm · Accelerator vendors

      Designs custom AI accelerators and infrastructure chips for hyperscalers, plus networking chips such as optical DSPs, retimers and Ethernet controllers for AI clusters. It ranks second to Broadcom in custom AI chips and competes with it directly to design hyperscalers’ accelerators.

    • mask blank

      Term

      mask blanks, EUV blank, EUV blanks, photomask blank, photomask blanks, blank plate, DUV blanks

      A mask blank is a photomask before any pattern is on it. It is a six-inch square of very flat glass carrying the film that the pattern will be cut into. For extreme ultraviolet that film sits on a mirror of about forty pairs of ultrathin layers, and a particle buried in the mirror cannot be repaired.

      The Japanese glassmaker AGC says only three firms supply EUV blanks, and AGC and Hoya, both Japanese, are two of them. AGC spent more than a decade meeting the blank’s requirements before it began mass production in 2017.

      Read it in Photomasks and Pellicles

    • mask shop

      Term

      mask shops, mask making, mask maker, mask makers

      A mask shop is the factory that turns a finished chip design into its set of photomasks. It writes each plate with an electron beam, inspects it and repairs it.

      No chip can be printed until its masks are made. Chipmakers such as TSMC and SMIC run shops of their own, and independents such as Photronics sell to them and to others.

      Read it in Photomasks and Pellicles

    • mask writer

      Term

      mask writers, multi-beam writer, multi-beam writers, electron-beam writer, e-beam writer, mask writing

      A mask writer is the machine that uses electrons to draw a chip’s pattern into the resist on a photomask blank. A single-beam writer flashes one shape at a time, while NuFlare’s multi-beam writer for the most advanced masks controls 260,000 beams at once.

      No new chip can be printed until its masks are written. In 2023 Intel said advanced EUV requires multi-beam mask writers and called Austria’s IMS Nanofabrication the established leader in them. Counting all electron-beam mask writers, CSET put IMS at 46.6 percent of 2025 sales and Japan’s NuFlare at 39.2 percent.

      Read it in Photomasks and Pellicles

    • mature node

      Term

      mature nodes, mature-node, mature logic, older nodes, older lines, trailing edge

      A mature node is an older chipmaking process, 28 nm and above, that has run for years and competes on price. Most of the world’s wafers come off these lines, making power chips, analog parts and microcontrollers.

      China held 33 percent of the world’s logic capacity at 28 nm and above in 2022. In the five years before May 2024, Chinese companies invested $63 billion in 73 fabs, mostly for chips above 28 nm, SIA and BCG reported.

      Read it in Foundries and Fabs

    • MediaTek

      Firm · Accelerator vendors

      聯發科技

      Best known for its smartphone chips, MediaTek also designs custom AI chips (ASICs) and works on Google’s TPU program. It has experience designing high-volume chips on advanced nodes.

    • memory bandwidth density

      Term

      bandwidth density, bandwidth-density

      Memory bandwidth density is how much data a memory stack can move each second divided by the area of its package or stack, in gigabytes per second per square millimeter. The December 2024 rule controls any stack above 2, and BIS said every HBM stack then in production exceeded that.

      One threshold catches every HBM stack in production, including stacks made outside the United States, so the control reaches all three makers, SK hynix, Samsung and Micron. A license exception still lets stacks below 3.3 go straight to a chip designer’s packaging site. HBM already packaged with a processor falls under the chip rules instead.

      Read it in Memory and HBM

    • memory wall

      Term

      The widening gap between how fast a processor can calculate and how fast memory can feed it numbers to work on. The cost of arithmetic has fallen faster than the cost of moving numbers.

      An AI chip reads its whole model from memory for each word it writes, so memory size and speed usually set how many people one chip can serve. Memory is also about half the cost of building an Nvidia B200, on Epoch AI’s estimate.

      Read it in Memory and HBM

    • Merck KGaA

      Firm · Chemicals and gases

      Its electronics division supplies deposition precursors, specialty gases, CMP slurries and dielectrics. Merck built the division around its acquisitions of Versum Materials and AZ Electronic Materials. It sells one of the broadest ranges of materials of any single supplier.

    • Meta MTIA 300

      AI chip

      MTIA 300 is Meta’s first training chip, built to train its ranking and recommendation models. The compute chiplet measures 25.6 by 31.4 mm and fills a full reticle, the largest area a lithography scanner can print in one exposure. It has a spare row of processing elements to improve yield, the share of chips that come out working. Two network chiplets of 25.6 by 9.3 mm carry the network interfaces, so data reaches the network without a hop over PCIe to a separate network card. Power is rated at 912 W, with 667 W typical. Meta names no foundry or node for the part, but its ISCA 2026 paper describes the package as CoWoS.

    • Meta MTIA 400

      AI chip

      Meta says it can ship a new chip roughly every six months. MTIA 400 is the second of four successive generations Meta described in March 2026. MTIA 450 doubles HBM bandwidth again, and Meta quotes MTIA 500 at 4.5 times the HBM bandwidth and 25 times the compute of MTIA 300. Broadcom supplies the XPU design platform, the advanced packaging and the Ethernet networking. Meta publishes no foundry, node, HBM generation, die area, transistor count, HBM capacity, HBM supplier, TDP or absolute performance for MTIA 400. It gives performance only as ratios to MTIA 300. The only absolute memory figure is in the companion MTIA 300 post, which gives 216 GB of HBM3E for MTIA 300.

    • Meta MTIA v2

      AI chip

      MTIA v2 has no HBM at all. It uses 128 GB of LPDDR5, the low-power memory used in phones and laptops, backed by 256 MB of on-chip SRAM. Its 204.8 GB/s of memory bandwidth is about a sixteenth of an H100’s. Meta made that memory choice deliberately for ranking and recommendation work, where the model is small and the traffic is enormous. Meta’s 2024 blog gives the chip’s power as 90 W, and its 2026 ISCA paper gives 85 W (65 W typical). Meta also publishes die details that almost no other vendor does. The die measures 25.6 by 16.4 mm (421 mm²) and holds 2.35 billion gates on TSMC 5 nm. Meta publishes no package type and no network for linking chips across servers, which fits a card that plugs into a server over PCIe. It names no memory supplier.

      Firm · Accelerator vendors

      Designs the MTIA inference accelerator for its recommendation and ranking workloads, built with Broadcom at TSMC. Meta is also one of the largest buyers of GPUs from outside chip vendors.

    • metal-oxide resist

      Term

      metal-oxide resists, metal oxide resist, tin-oxide resist, metal-oxide EUV photoresist

      A metal-oxide resist is a photoresist built on clusters with a tin-oxide core. It absorbs more extreme ultraviolet light than a chemically amplified resist. That helps because an EUV dose arrives as relatively few photons.

      Resist makers aim it at High-NA tools and the tightest pitches. The Japanese resist maker JSR agreed in 2021 to buy Inpria, an Oregon maker of these resists. In 2024 a company owned by a Japanese state-backed fund took 84.36 percent of JSR.

      Read it in Chemicals, Gases and Photoresist

    • MetaX

      Firm · Accelerator vendors

      沐曦集成电路

      A Chinese designer of general-purpose GPUs, whose Xiyun and Xisi lines are built for AI training and inference in Chinese data centers. It offers a CUDA-compatible software stack.

    • METI

      Export control

      Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, Japan’s Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry

      METI is Japan’s Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, the ministry that writes Japan’s export controls and funds its chip industry. It put advanced chipmaking equipment under export license from July 2023. It also supports the chipmaker Rapidus and new capacity for mask blanks, the glass plates that photomasks are made from.

      Japan’s controls apply to every destination and name no country, and METI decides them.

      Read it in Who Controls the Chain

    • metrology

      Term

      process control, when grouped with inspection, metrology and inspection, inspection tools

      Measuring what a factory actually built: how wide a printed line came out, how thick a film is, whether this layer sits exactly on top of the last one. Inspection is the related job of finding flaws.

      A fab that cannot buy sensitive inspection tools finds fewer of the defects that lower its yield, so its yield rises more slowly. KLA held 56.8 percent of the market for these tools in 2025, by CSET’s count.

      Read it in Metrology and Inspection

    • microbump

      Term

      microbumps, solder bump, solder bumps, bumps, bump, bump metrology

      A microbump is a dot of solder that joins a die to the interposer or substrate beneath it. In Intel’s 2.5D packages microbumps sit 36 microns apart, less than half a hair’s width. Each one is an electrical connection that has to survive as the package heats and cools.

      Their spacing limits how many connections fit between stacked or neighboring chips. Hybrid bonding, which joins copper straight to copper, would pack connections far closer, but it is not yet ready for HBM.

      Read it in Advanced Packaging

      Firm · Memory

      The only American maker of leading-edge DRAM and the third HBM supplier, with fabs in the US, Japan, Taiwan and Singapore. It has CHIPS Act support for new capacity in Idaho and New York.

      Firm · Test

      株式会社日本マイクロニクス

      Designs the Maia accelerator family and the Cobalt Arm server CPU for Microsoft’s Azure cloud. It also designs the ‘sidekick’ racks that sit beside the servers and supply the liquid cooling they need. Maia 200 is the current generation.

    • Microsoft Maia 100

      AI chip

      Maia 100 is Microsoft’s first accelerator. It is also the first silicon anywhere to implement the Microscaling data format, in which small blocks of numbers share one scale factor, and that format later became the MX standard. Microsoft published the cooling design in detail, down to the sidekick heat exchanger that sits beside the rack. It later described the chip itself in its Inside Maia 100 post and at the Hot Chips 2024 conference. By Microsoft’s own figures, the chip is a die of about 820 mm² on TSMC N5 with four HBM2E stacks, 64 GB at 1.8 TB/s, on CoWoS-S. Microsoft’s Azure post of 3 April 2024 dates the announcement to November 2023, the date shown above. Epoch AI records the part at August 2024, when Microsoft presented it at Hot Chips. Microsoft designed the chip for up to 700 W and provisions it at 500 W, the figure shown.

    • Microsoft Maia 200

      AI chip

      Maia 200 is the exception among 2026 flagships. It uses only Ethernet, its network interface (NIC) is built into the die, it needs no proprietary scale-up cabling, and a two-tier network links up to 6,144 accelerators. Microsoft publishes over 140 billion transistors on TSMC’s N3 process, 216 GB of HBM3E at 7 TB/s, 272 MB of on-die SRAM and a 750 W power rating for the chip. It publishes no die area, packaging technology or HBM stack count, and its architecture deep dive names no CoWoS variant. Epoch AI’s die figure of roughly 820 mm² belongs to Maia 100, the earlier part. No allowed source publishes a Maia 200 die area.

    • mm²

      Term

      mm2, square millimeters, square millimeter

      mm² means square millimeters, the unit chip areas are given in. A lithography scanner prints at most 858 mm² in one shot, and each compute die in an Nvidia B200 is about 800 mm². In 2028 TSMC plans to start making chip packages whose base layer, the wiring that links the chips, covers 14 scanner shots.

      Yield, the share of dies that work, falls as die area grows, so the cost of each working chip rises faster than its area.

      Read it in The Economics of AI Chips

    • model weights

      Export control

      weights, frontier model weights, trained weights

      Model weights are the billions of numbers that make up a trained AI model. They are the file that runs on the chips, so copying the weights copies the model.

      A chip reads the model’s weights from memory for each word it writes, so bigger models need more HBM. The AI Diffusion rule also made frontier model weights a controlled item, ECCN 4E091.

      Read it in Who Controls the Chain

      MOFCOM is China’s Ministry of Commerce, the ministry that writes and administers China’s own export controls. Its notices put gallium, germanium and seven rare earths under license. In December 2024 it banned exports of gallium, germanium, antimony and superhard materials to the United States.

      China’s retaliation targets inputs such as these minerals, and MOFCOM signs each notice.

      Read it in Who Controls the Chain

    • multipatterning

      Term

      double patterning, quadruple patterning, self-aligned double patterning, self-aligned quadruple patterning, SADP, SAQP, LELE, multiple patterning, multi-patterning, several passes, several exposures, multiply exposed, DUV multipatterning

      Building one chip layer in several patterning steps, because a single exposure cannot print lines that close together. It comes in two kinds. Litho-etch multipatterning splits the layer’s pattern across two or three masks, then prints and etches each part separately. Self-aligned double or quadruple patterning prints one coarser pattern, then deposits and etches thin spacer films along its edges to halve or quarter the line spacing. Cut masks then remove the parts of lines the circuit does not need.

      SMIC makes its 7 nm-class chips without extreme ultraviolet machines by multipatterning on deep ultraviolet tools. TSMC’s first 7 nm process and Intel 7 were also made without extreme ultraviolet light. Every extra mask or spacer step adds cost and machine time, and each extra litho-etch exposure adds a chance that parts of the layer misalign.

      Read it in Lithography

  • N

    • Nan Ya PCB

      Firm · Substrates and PCBs

      南亞電路板

      Produces ABF and BT IC substrates and high-layer-count printed circuit boards, and is one of the main IC substrate makers worldwide.

    • NAND

      Term

      3D NAND, NAND flash, flash memory, 128-layer NAND

      NAND is the memory that keeps data when the power is off. It is the storage inside a phone, a laptop drive or a data center disk. 3D NAND stacks its cells in many layers, made by etching holes far deeper than they are wide. It is slow next to DRAM and is not used inside an AI accelerator.

      Under the October 2022 US rules, items subject to US export rules bound for a fab in China that makes NAND with 128 or more layers need a license. The proposed MATCH Act would name YMTC, a Chinese NAND maker, in the law itself.

      Read it in Memory and HBM

    • nanometer

      Term

      nm, nanometers, microns, micrometer, micrometers, angstrom, angstroms, picometer, picometers

      A nanometer is a billionth of a meter. A micron, or micrometer, is a thousand nanometers, an angstrom is a tenth of a nanometer, and a picometer is a thousandth. Lithography light is measured in nanometers, package bumps in microns, and mirror flatness in picometers.

      Node names such as 2 nm no longer describe any feature that size, but the physical limits of printing and stacking are still measured in these units.

      Read it in Lithography

      Firm · Memory

      南亞科技

      Taiwan’s DRAM maker, producing commodity and specialty DRAM at mature nodes. It does not make HBM and is a generation or more behind the three leading DRAM makers.

      沪硅产业

      China’s state-backed silicon wafer group, which owns Shanghai Zing Semiconductor (300 mm wafers) and Okmetic in Finland (specialty wafers). It is China’s domestic alternative to Japanese wafer supply.

      China’s largest semiconductor equipment maker, with plasma etch, deposition (PVD, CVD and ALD), furnace and cleaning tools. As Chinese fabs replaced foreign tools with local ones, Naura rose into the world’s top ten chipmaking equipment suppliers by sales in 2025. That year three Chinese firms made the global top 20, up from one in 2022.

    • neon

      neon gas, semiconductor-grade neon

      Neon, mixed with krypton or argon and fluorine, is the gas inside the lasers that give deep ultraviolet scanners their light. A fab uses it by the cylinder, and those scanners cannot print without it.

      Ukraine supplied about 70 percent of the world’s neon before Russia invaded in 2022. Many chipmakers had added to their gas stockpiles after Russia annexed Crimea in 2014, and several reported adequate supplies from China.

      Read it in Chemicals, Gases and Photoresist

      Nitrogen trifluoride is a gas that cleans process chambers between wafers. Split apart in a plasma, it releases fluorine that scours the deposits off the inside of the chamber.

      A shortage of any one chemical can stop a fab. SK Specialty of South Korea has made nitrogen trifluoride since 2001, when it became the first company to produce the gas there.

      Read it in Chemicals, Gases and Photoresist

In August 2025 it decided to expand glass fiber cloth production at its Fukushima Enterprise Center, with the added output starting in the fourth quarter of its fiscal 2026. It says Chinese and Taiwanese companies are aggressively catching up with it in special glass.

    • nm-class

      Term

      5 nm-class, 7 nm-class, 2 nm-class, nanometer-class, nm class

      Nm-class, as in 7 nm-class, means a process roughly as dense as the foundries’ 7 nm generation. The label is used when a maker’s own name for the node is different.

      China’s SMIC builds its 7 nm-class processes without extreme ultraviolet machines, and its most advanced, N+3, reaches the density of TSMC’s 6 nm-class process.

      Read it in Foundries and Fabs

    • node

      Term

      process node, technology node, for example N2 or 18A, nodes

      The name a foundry gives one generation of its manufacturing process. The number in the name no longer measures anything on the chip. SMIC’s N+3, a 7 nm-class process, spaces its narrowest wires closer together than Intel’s Panther Lake chips on 18A do.

      Comparing two foundries by node name says little. Each foundry also picks its own baseline for the density gains it claims.

      Read it in Foundries and Fabs

      Supplies optical critical dimension scatterometry and X-ray metrology used to measure three-dimensional structures such as gate-all-around nanosheets and high aspect ratio memory holes.
